html:
The Nuxalk, also called the Bella Coola, are a First Nation of the central coast of British Columbia, centred on the Bella Coola valley and its long inlets. They speak a Salishan language that is cut off by distance from the other Salish languages to the south.

They lived from salmon and eulachon, a small oily fish whose rendered grease they traded inland along "grease trails" to the Dakelh (Carrier). Their carved masks and their potlatch feasts are well known. Their coastal neighbours are the Heiltsuk and the Wuikinuxv.

In 1793 Alexander Mackenzie followed a grease trail down to Nuxalk villages and reached the Pacific, the first European to cross North America north of Mexico. A smallpox epidemic in the 1860s killed a large share of the people, and survivors gathered at the village of Bella Coola.
